findings.title: Denial cache key collides with the permission cache key
findings.body: userPermDenialCacheKey is namespace+".perm_"+userUID+"_"+action+"_"+name+"_"+parent. userPermCacheKey is namespace+".perm_"+userUID+"_"+action. The prefixes are the same, and both are stored in the same underlying cache. Underscore-joined fields with no separator escaping are also ambiguous: names containing underscores could collide with other users' or actions' keys. Use a distinct prefix such as ".perm_denied_" and an unambiguous separator.

findings.title: Denial cache blocks newly granted access for the TTL, defeating the PR goal
findings.body: A denial is cached for 30s per (user, action, name, folder). If a check runs just before a resource is created or permissions are granted, for example a creator checking a dashboard before the permission row is visible, access stays denied for the full TTL even though the permission now exists in the DB. The fallback requery is skipped on every denial-cache hit. Nothing invalidates the entry when permissions change.

findings.title: Denied checks on cached permissions requery the DB each time
findings.body: When the cached permissions do not allow the request, the code always calls getIdentityPermissions, which hits the DB. The denial cache is only populated after that call succeeds, so a burst of concurrent denied checks for different resources causes a DB query per distinct resource. Distinct names also each get their own denial key, so the cache gives little protection against scanning patterns. Metrics also count a cache miss in this case.

findings.title: Errors from the cached-permission lookup are ignored
findings.body: getCachedIdentityPermissions can return a real error, such as a failure in GetUserIdentifiers. Check treats every error as a cache miss and falls through, which is acceptable. However, the err variable is shadowed inside the if block, and List does the same. The resulting double lookup of identifiers is a minor inefficiency.

findings.title: Missing test that a denial is cached after a DB-checked deny
findings.body: The tests never verify that Check populates permDenialCache after a denial, or that a repeat call avoids the DB. The 'should return permissions from cache' case in getUserPermissions was removed without equivalent coverage of the singleflight and DB paths.
